Hadhrat Umar (RA) Endures Hardships and difficulties

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates, "When (my father) Hadhrat Umar (RA) accepted Islaam, he asked, 'Which person of the Quraysh is the best informant?' When he was told that it was Jameel bin Ma'mar Jumhi, he went to him early in the morning. I followed my father to see what he was doing. Although I was then still a child, I understood everything I saw. When he arrived, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'O Jameel! Do you know that I have accepted Islaam and entered into the religion of Muhammad ﷺ?' By Allaah! Jameel gave no response and left, pulling his shawl along with him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) followed him and I followed my father."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates further that Jameel arrived at the door of the Masjidul Haraam as the people were sitting in their gatherings around the Kabah. He then screamed at the top of his voice, "O assembly of the Quraysh! The son of Khattaab has become a heretic!" Standing behind him, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "He is lying! The fact is that I have accepted Islaam and I testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is Allaah's Rasul." The people then attacked Hadhrat Umar (RA) and they continued fighting him until the sun stood above their heads (midday). Exhausted, Hadhrat Umar (RA) then sat down and the people stood over him. He said, "Do as you please. I swear by Allaah that we now number three hundred strong and we shall either leave Makkah for you or you leave it for us."

As they were talking, an old man from the Quraysh arrived wearing clothes made in Yemen with a striped upper garment. He asked, "What is the matter with you lot?" When they told him that Hadhrat Umar (RA) had accepted Islaam, he said, "Then stop this. Do you think that the Banu Adi tribe (to which he belongs) will hand their man over to you just like that? Leave the man alone." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "By Allaah! The people then (disappeared so fast that it) seemed as if a sheet had been lifted from Hadhrat Umar (RA). After migrating to Madinah, I once asked my father, 'Dear father! Who was that old man who drove those people away from you in Makkah when they were fighting with you on the day you accepted Islaam?' He replied, 'That man, dear son, was Aas bin Waa'il Sahmi.'"[^1]
